newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria '96 inflation 311 pct, highest since '91.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria '96 inflation 311 pct, highest since '91.

text.p: Bulgaria's December consumer price inflation was 310.8 percent year-on-year, the second largest year-over-year increase since the country launched market reforms in 1990, National Statistics Institute (NSI) said.

"The sharp lev fall against the dollar, the decline of output and exports and surging prices of fuels and electricity boosted annual inflation to its highest level since 1991," NSI director Zahari Karamfilov told a news conference.
The previous year-on-year record high of 473.7 percent was in December 1991, figures showed.

Monthly December inflation accelerated by 26.9 percent to post the third largest record monthly increase, following a 122.9-percent surge in February 1991 and a 50.5-percent jump in March 1991, the NSI said.
BULGARIAN CONSUMER PRICES DEC NOV DEC'95

The lev fell 6.6 times against the dollar in December year-on-year, boosting prices of imported goods 5.5 times on average, the NSI said. The lev traded around 510 per dollar at the end of December last year.

Depending on the grade, petrol prices were 602 to 606 percent higher in December 1996 than a year earlier, diesel prices increased 617 percent and electricity for households was 507 percent more expensive, NSI figures showed.
The NSI said that at the end of 1996, prices were 306 times higher than in May 1990 when it began to calculate consumer price inflation. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
